passages.provision_quote: 4. For personal property that is initially classified during or after tax year 2022 as class one, paragraph 8, 9, 10 or 13 pursuant to section 42-12001 personal property that is initially classified during or after tax year 2022 as class two (P) pursuant to section 42-12002 and personal property that is acquired during or after tax year 2022 and initially classified during or after tax year 2022 as class six pursuant to section 42-12006, paragraph 2 or 3, the assessor shall use a valuation factor of two and one-half percent.
passages.note: Chapter 103 sets a uniform depreciation/valuation schedule for all qualifying business personal property, not a company-specific incentive, matching the annex's 'uniform tax change' hard case.
Weninger voted Yea on HB2822's House Final Reading, but the bill is a uniform personal-property valuation rule, not a business-attraction incentive.
Weninger is listed as prime sponsor of HB2822, which the Governor signed as Chapter 103; the bill's content is a general valuation-schedule change, not an employer-attraction incentive.

rows.reasoning: HB 2822 (2022), which Weninger prime-sponsored, voted Yea on, and saw signed as Chapter 103, amends the depreciation schedule used to value personal property for property-tax purposes — a uniform rule applied to all qualifying business personal property, not a tax break, subsidy, or incentive aimed at attracting a specific company. The annex's hard case treats 'a change to how all business property is valued' as tax policy, not an attraction incentive, so this evidence is adjacent to every rung on this ladder.
